data.why: No bundled example spectrum ships with the repo, so a single-column histogram CSV (counts-per-channel, no header) was synthesized matching the documented 'ready-to-use histogram' format, with a decaying Compton-like continuum, three Gaussian photopeaks at channels corresponding to Am-241 (59.5 keV), Ba-133 (356 keV) and Cs-137 (662 keV) under an assumed linear calibration (E = 5 + 2.2*channel), plus a dead channel (0 counts at ch 50) and a cosmic-ray-like outlier spike (480 counts at ch 200) for the agent to notice and exclude during peak-finding.

goals: Import a histogram spectrum file and view the raw counts-vs-channel plot
Perform an n-th degree polynomial energy calibration by assigning known gamma-ray energies to peak channels
Run Gaussian correlation peak-finding to auto-detect candidate photopeaks and flag the non-physical outlier
Identify isotopes present by matching detected peak energies against the built-in isotope energy library
Export the calibrated, annotated spectrum as an NPES JSON/XML file or an interactive graph

review.summary: This is a well-built tree of offline gamma-spectrum analysis: calibration, peak finding and isotope matching are in clear phases, the general labels are domain-neutral, and every screen I opened matches its node. It still needs fixes before filing: it leaves out live serial acquisition and the all-in-one JSON/XML session export, which the README presents as core, and it overstates the result by claiming automatic Cs-137 identification and an exported annotated spectrum.
